bug_semantics: An attacker-controlled WEBSERVICE() formula can name a URL on an allowed hostname that returns an HTTP redirect to an internal or otherwise forbidden destination. The implementation validates only the initial URL's parsed hostname, then passes that URL to PHP's HTTP stream wrapper, whose redirect following is enabled by default; no redirected hop is checked against the domain whitelist, so the response from the forbidden destination is returned as the cell value.
flaw_origin: Commit 84747121a19055c17ed7042429cd31da5020c094 replaced the configurable PSR HTTP client path with file_get_contents(), added a one-time hostname whitelist check, and constructed an HTTP stream context without follow_location=0 or per-hop validation. That atomic combination created the advisory's redirect-based whitelist bypass; the subsequent instance-property refactor preserved it.

evidence: The first-party GitHub advisory https://github.com/PHPOffice/PhpSpreadsheet/security/advisories/GHSA-6hq5-7373-42rg identifies CVE-2026-59931, describes the initial-host-only whitelist check plus automatically followed redirects, names 7ef7b25e8548a6ded79dac74e2e2c7acdac38d8d as the fix, and is not withdrawn.

The CVE.org/CVE Services record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-59931 is PUBLISHED and describes the same PhpSpreadsheet WEBSERVICE domain-whitelist redirect bypass; it is not rejected or disputed.

git show 84747121a19055c17ed7042429cd31da5020c094 shows src/PhpSpreadsheet/Calculation/Web/Service.php lines 31-51 parsing and checking only the initial host, then creating an HTTP context containing only user_agent and calling file_get_contents($url, false, $ctx), with no follow_location disable or redirected-hop revalidation.

Direct parent-tree verification against f2acc0afbbf113ad7547effb7b0e8c9dba713240 found getDomainWhiteList, file_get_contents, and follow_location all absent from src/PhpSpreadsheet/Calculation/Web/Service.php; the parent used a configurable PSR client and therefore lacks the specific one-time-whitelist-plus-PHP-wrapper mechanism introduced by the BIC.

reasoning: The advisory is a real, published SSRF issue, not a withdrawn or rejected report. The defining flaw is not WEBSERVICE's older general ability to make outbound requests; it is the false security boundary created when PR #4751 checked the initial hostname but then used a redirect-following PHP stream without checking later hops. The preserved PR history makes 84747121a19055c17ed7042429cd31da5020c094 smaller than the merge aggregate and shows it first wrote that exact mechanism. Its immediate parent lacks both the whitelist and file_get_contents path, satisfying parent absence. Later commit 9bc3a73ba4e0fd93d10f20c63829de3142143fbb changes whitelist ownership but does not introduce the redirect behavior. The vendor's version ranges also cover older unrestricted-WEBSERVICE releases, while the exact whitelist-bypass mechanism reaches the maintained lines through the 5.4.0 change and corresponding backports; all advertised patched boundaries contain a direct follow_location-disable fix. Finally, only the atomic BIC commit object controls AI attribution: it has human author/committer identities and no AI or bot marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
